card.name: "To" in worsening symptom progressions
card.fires_on: The word "to" right after "progress", "progressing" or "ranging from X", leading into a more severe outcome such as coma or stupor. This mostly occurs in overdose descriptions.

modes.label: Ranging from X to Y
modes.description: "to" after a mild sign, introducing the severe end of a range.
modes.example: central nervous system depression ranging from drowsiness<< to>> coma.

modes.label: Progressing to
modes.description: "to" after "progress" or "progressing", introducing a worse state.
modes.example: respiratory depression which may progress<< to>> Cheyne-Stokes respiration

modes.label: Acute before renal failure
modes.description: A rarer case: "acute" after "reversible", before kidney failure.
modes.example: resulted in reversible<< acute>> renal failure in two of four healthy volunteers

card.plain: It marks the point in an overdose description where symptoms are said to worsen toward a severe outcome like coma.
